classification.difficultyReason: Convert lengths to common units, distinguish plants from intervals, and multiply by the number of rows.

content.prompt: A man plants 12 rows of beans in rows that are 10 m long. The plants in each row are spaced 50 cm apart. If the first and last plants in a row are 25 cm from the ends of the row, what is the total number of plants?

answer.worked:
Each row is $1000\text{ cm}$ long.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Distance between first and last plants}&=1000-25-25\\\text{Distance between first and last plants}&=950\text{ cm}\\\text{Number of intervals per row}&=950\div50\\\text{Number of intervals per row}&=19\\\text{Number of plants per row}&=19+1\\\text{Number of plants per row}&=20\\\text{Total number of plants}&=12\times20\\\text{Total number of plants}&=240\end{align*}$$

There is one more plant than the number of intervals between plants.
